newsitem.title: USA: Saudi barley tender results seen Wednesday - trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley tender results seen Wednesday - trade.

text.p: Results of a Saudi Arabian barley tender may be known as early as Wednesday, with the European Union and Australia likely to take the lion's share of the business, Canadian grain export sources said.
Saudi Arabia on Tuesday was seeking 1.2 million tonnes of feed barley for January and February shipment.
Several Canadian grain traders said Canada was not likely to get much of the business because of weather-related loading delays at Vancouver and the lack of barley in port.
There were five ships loading and 25 waiting to load on Canada's west coast on Monday, with 20 days the longest wait.
"I think Canada would benefit very little from the tender. I know the (Canadian) Wheat Board is not offering," one Canadian grain trader said.
As a result, traders said they expected Canada to get only about 100,000 to 250,000 tonnes out of the expected sale.
"There is a problem getting the barley to the port, and over the holidays harsh winter conditions shut down the Canadian rail lines," a second Canadian trader said.

A third Canadian trader said some of the Saudi business could turn out to be March shipment. He said 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes of the business could go to Canada, with Australia and the European Union rumored to get the balance.
The Canadian traders disagreed on the price of the deal but said a range of US$139-145 per tonne FOB was likely.
